chunks: And the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said:

There is no salat (prayer) whose time arrives except that an angel calls out before the people: 'O people, rise to the fires which you have kindled upon your backs, and extinguish them with your salat (prayer).'

key_terms.أَوْقَدْتُمُوهَا: you kindled it, meaning you yourselves caused these fires through your deeds
key_terms.بِصَلَاتِكُمْ: with your salat (prayer), indicating prayer as the means of extinguishing them
key_terms.صَلَاةٍ: salat (prayer), the prescribed act of worship performed at its appointed time
key_terms.ظُهُورِكُمْ: your backs, expressing that these burdens are carried by the people themselves
key_terms.فَأَطْفِئُوهَا: so extinguish it, a command to remove those fires through worship
key_terms.مَلَكٌ: an angel, a heavenly caller announcing the time and urging response
key_terms.نِيرَانِكُمُ: your fires, a metaphor for the harmful consequences of sins
key_terms.وَقْتُهَا: its appointed time, the fixed moment when the prayer becomes due

ai.seo_question: How does salat (prayer) extinguish the spiritual effects of sins according to hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith urges believers to hasten to salat (prayer) when its time enters, portraying prayer as a means of extinguishing the spiritual consequences of sins. It emphasizes the urgent, purifying, and protective role of salat (prayer) in a believer's life.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
"There is no prayer whose time arrives except that an angel calls out in front of the people,
'O’ people, stand up to extinguish the fires you have ignited upon your backs with your prayers.'".
